learn.hook: Every drawing in geometry is built from tiny dots and straight paths. Let's meet the building blocks!
points: A point marks an exact spot. We name it with a capital letter, like point P.
A line segment is the straight path between two points. It has two endpoints and a length we can measure, like segment AB.
A line goes on forever in both directions. Through two points, exactly one line can pass.
A ray starts at one point and goes on forever in one direction. Ray OA starts at O and passes through A.
An angle is made by two rays that start from the same point. That point is the vertex, and the rays are the arms.

example.q: A figure starts at point O, passes through point A and goes on forever. Name it.
steps: It has one starting point (O) and no end.
A figure with one endpoint that goes on forever is a ray.
We write the starting point first.

learn.reallife: A torch beam is like a ray, the edge of your ruler is a line segment, and the tip of a pencil marks a point.

games.title: Match the real thing to the geometry word
pairs: A straight path with no ends at all
Two arms of an open pair of scissors

games.title: True or false?
items: A line segment has two endpoints.
It starts at one point and stops at another.
A ray has two endpoints.
A ray has only one endpoint; it goes on forever the other way.
Exactly one line can pass through two given points.
Two points fix one straight line.
We can measure the length of a line with a ruler.
A line goes on forever. Only a line segment has a length.
Ray PQ and ray QP are the same ray.
Ray PQ starts at P, ray QP starts at Q. They point in opposite directions.
Many lines can pass through a single point.
You can draw lines through one point in every direction.

quiz.q: How many endpoints does a line segment have?
quiz.explain: A line segment starts at one point and ends at another, so it has 2 endpoints.
steps: A line segment starts at one point and stops at another.
Each of those points is an endpoint.
Count them: start + end = 2.
So a line segment has 2 endpoints.
Answer: 2
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a segment with a ray (1 endpoint) or a line (0 endpoints)

quiz.q: Which figure starts at one point and goes on forever in one direction?
quiz.explain: A ray has one starting point and no end in the other direction.
steps: A line goes on forever in both directions; a segment stops at both ends.
A ray has one starting point and goes on forever in one direction.
A point has no length at all.
So the answer is ray.
Answer: Ray
quiz.mistake: Thinks a line has a starting point

quiz.q: In ray XY, which point is the starting point?
quiz.explain: A ray is always named starting point first, so ray XY starts at X and passes through Y.
steps: Rule: a ray is named with its starting point first.
In ray XY, the first letter is X.
So the ray starts at X and passes through Y.
Answer: X
quiz.mistake: Does not know that the first letter names the starting point of a ray

quiz.q: Points A, B and C lie on one straight line in that order. How many different line segments can you name using these points?
quiz.explain: The segments are AB, BC and AC. AB and BA are the same segment, so there are 3.
steps: AB
BC
AC (the whole length)
Total = 3
Answer: 3
quiz.mistake: Forgets the long segment AC (2), or counts AB and BA as different (6)

quiz.q: How many straight lines can pass through two different points P and Q?
quiz.explain: Two points fix exactly one straight line.
steps: Through two different points we can draw only one straight line.
Any other line through P would miss Q.
So exactly one line passes through P and Q.
Answer: Exactly one
quiz.mistake: Thinks of curved paths, which are not straight lines

quiz.q: An angle is made by...
options: two rays with the same starting point
quiz.explain: Two rays starting from one point (the vertex) form an angle. The rays are its arms.
steps: An angle has a vertex and two arms.
The arms are two rays starting from the same point (the vertex).
Two points, one segment or two lines that never meet do not make an angle.
So an angle is made by two rays with the same starting point.
Answer: two rays with the same starting point
quiz.mistake: Does not know that the arms of an angle must meet at a vertex

quiz.q: Joseph marks 4 points, with no three on one straight line, and joins every pair. How many line segments does he draw?
quiz.explain: The first point joins 3 others, the next joins 2 new ones, then 1: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.
steps: Answer: 6
quiz.mistake: Counts each segment twice (12) or draws only the outline (4)

quiz.q: Which of these can be measured with a ruler?
quiz.explain: Only a line segment has two ends, so only it has a fixed length.
steps: A ruler measures length between two ends.
A line has no ends, and a ray has only one end, so neither has a fixed length.
A point has no length.
Only line segment AB, with two endpoints, can be measured.
Answer: Line segment AB
quiz.mistake: Thinks a line or ray has a fixed length

teach.ask: Gappu is confused: 'A line, a ray and a line segment all look straight! How are they different?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Segment: two ends. Ray: one end, goes on one way. Line: no ends, goes on both ways. Got it!
teach.nudge: But how many ends does each one have, and which way does it keep going?

revise.summary: A point marks an exact spot, a line segment joins two points, a line goes on forever both ways and a ray starts at one point and goes on forever one way. An angle is made by two rays starting from the same point.
focus: Tell a segment (2 endpoints), a ray (1 starting point) and a line (no endpoints) apart
Name a ray with its starting point first
Count the segments that can be named from points on a line or joined in pairs
Know that only a line segment can be measured with a ruler
remember: Through two points, exactly one line can pass
Ray OA starts at O and passes through A
An angle: two rays from the same point; that point is the vertex, the rays are the arms
traps: A line has no starting point; don't confuse it with a ray
Don't forget the long segment AC when A, B, C are on a line, and don't count AB and BA as two
A line or ray has no fixed length; only a segment can be measured

learn.hook: Fold a paper and the crease is a perfect straight segment. No ruler needed!
points: Fold a paper so that two dots touch the crease: the crease between them is a line segment. Any other route between the dots is longer.
A line can be named by any two points on it (line AB) or by one small letter (line l, line m).
We can never draw a complete line, because it never ends. We draw a part and put arrowheads at both ends.
In a figure, read carefully: two endpoints means a segment; one arrowhead means a ray; arrowheads at both ends mean a line.
Rough figures from statements: 'P lies on line l' means draw line l with a dot P on it; 'ray OA' means start at O and go through A.

example.q: Points A, B, C lie on line m in that order. Name the line in three ways and list the segments.
steps: Line m can be called line AB, line BC or line AC (any two of its points).
Segments: AB, BC and AC.
There are 3 segments.
example.answer: Line m = line AB = line AC; segments AB, BC, AC

learn.reallife: A stretched clothesline between two poles is a segment; a crease in a folded chapati wrapper is a segment too.

games.title: Segment, ray or line?
items: Has 2 endpoints
Edge of a table
Has 1 endpoint
Torch beam from a torch
Ray OP
No endpoints at all
Line l
Arrowheads at both ends

games.title: Naming rules
items: Line AB and line BA are the same line.
A line has no start, so the order does not matter.
We can draw a complete line on a big chart paper.
A line never ends, so we only draw part of it.
A small letter like l can name a line.
Lines are often named l, m, n.
The paper-fold crease between two dots is the shortest route between them.
A straight segment is the shortest path.
Segment PQ has arrowheads at both ends.
A segment has two endpoints and no arrowheads.

quiz.q: Points P, Q and R lie on line n. Which is another correct name for line n?
quiz.explain: Any two points on the line name it, so line QR is line n.
steps: Any two points on a line can be used to name it.
Q and R both lie on line n.
So line QR is another name for line n.
Ray QR stops at Q on one side, so it is not the whole line.
Answer: Line QR
quiz.mistake: Mixes up line names with ray or segment names

quiz.q: Why do we draw arrowheads on both ends of a line?
options: To show it goes on endlessly in both directions
To show it is 10 cm long
quiz.explain: A line never ends, so arrowheads show that it continues both ways.
steps: A line never ends.
Arrowheads at both ends show it continues endlessly both ways.
It does not show a length or a starting point.
So the arrowheads show it goes on endlessly in both directions.
Answer: To show it goes on endlessly in both directions
quiz.mistake: Thinks a drawn line is the whole line

quiz.q: Manu walks from his house to the shop. Which route is the shortest?
options: A curved path around the park
The straight path joining the two places
quiz.explain: The line segment joining two points is the shortest path between them.
steps: The shortest path between two points is the line segment joining them.
Zig-zag and curved paths are longer.
So the paths are not all the same.
The straight path is the shortest.
Answer: The straight path joining the two places
quiz.mistake: Thinks all routes are equally long

quiz.q: Four points A, B, C, D lie on one line in that order. How many line segments can be named using these points?
quiz.explain: AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD: 6 segments.
steps: From A: AB, AC, AD (3)
From B: BC, BD (2)
From C: CD (1)
Answer: 6
quiz.mistake: Counts only the small pieces AB, BC, CD

quiz.q: A figure has one endpoint O and passes through T with an arrowhead after T. What is it?
quiz.explain: It starts at O and goes on through T, so it is ray OT.
steps: The figure has one endpoint O.
It goes through T and keeps going (arrowhead after T).
One endpoint and endless in one direction = a ray, named starting point first.
So it is ray OT.
Answer: Ray OT
quiz.mistake: Writes the starting point last

quiz.q: Riya reads: 'Draw line l and mark a point A that is NOT on it.' Which drawing is right?
options: A dot A sitting on line l
A dot A away from line l
quiz.explain: Point A must be outside the line, so the dot is away from line l.
steps: The instruction says A is NOT on line l.
So the dot A must be drawn away from the line.
A dot on the line, crossing lines or a ray do not follow the instruction.
So the right drawing has dot A away from line l.
Answer: A dot A away from line l
quiz.mistake: Misses the word NOT

quiz.q: How many lines pass through the two points X and Y, and how many through X alone?
options: One through X and Y; endlessly many through X alone
quiz.explain: Exactly one line passes through two points, but endlessly many can pass through one point.
steps: Through two points X and Y: exactly one line.
Through one point X: we can turn the line in any direction, so endlessly many lines.
So: one through X and Y; endlessly many through X alone.
Answer: One through X and Y; endlessly many through X alone
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the two cases

quiz.q: A line segment AB is 7 cm long. Point C is on AB so that AC = 3 cm. What is CB?
quiz.explain: CB = AB − AC = 7 − 3 = 4 cm.
steps: C lies on AB, so AC + CB = AB.
CB = AB − AC = 7 − 3.
So CB = 4 cm.
Answer: 4 cm
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracting

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'I drew a long line on the wall. Did I draw the whole line?'
teach.praise: Tweet! A line never ends, so we draw only part of it with arrowheads.

revise.summary: A line can be named by any two points on it or by one small letter, and it is drawn with arrowheads at both ends because it never ends. The straight path (a line segment) is the shortest route between two points.
focus: Name one line in different ways using points on it
Read figures: two endpoints = segment, one arrowhead = ray, arrowheads at both ends = line
Draw rough figures from statements, reading words like NOT carefully
Find a missing part of a segment by subtracting
remember: Line m = line AB = line AC when A, B, C lie on line m
Through two points: exactly one line; through one point: endlessly many lines
The straight path between two points is the shortest route
traps: A drawn line is only a part of the whole line
With 4 points on a line there are 6 segments, not just the 3 small pieces
If AB = 7 cm and AC = 3 cm, CB = 4 cm: subtract, don't add

learn.hook: Scissors, a compass and a half-open door all hide an angle. Can you name them?
points: An angle has a vertex (the common starting point) and two arms (the two rays).
We name an angle with three letters, the vertex in the middle: ∠ABC has vertex B and arms BA and BC. ∠CBA is the same angle.
If many angles share one vertex, the name ∠B is not clear. Use three letters to say exactly which angle you mean.
Angles are all around: open scissors, a compass, an opening door, a book, a clock's hands.
Rays from one point make many angles: 3 rays from O (OA, OB, OC) make ∠AOB, ∠BOC and ∠AOC.

example.q: Rays OP, OQ, OR, OS start from O, in that order. Name all the angles.
steps: From OP: ∠POQ, ∠POR, ∠POS (3)
From OQ: ∠QOR, ∠QOS (2)
From OR: ∠ROS (1)
Total 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 angles

learn.reallife: A ceiling fan's blades meet at the centre making angles, and the hands of a clock form an angle at the centre.

items.text: The two rays of an angle are its ___
3 rays from one point make ___ angles

quiz.q: In ∠PQR, which point is the vertex?
quiz.explain: The middle letter is the vertex, so it is Q.
steps: Rule: in a three-letter angle name, the middle letter is the vertex.
In ∠PQR the middle letter is Q.
P and R are points on the arms.
So the vertex is Q.
Answer: Q
quiz.mistake: Takes the first letter as the vertex

quiz.q: Which name is the same as ∠XYZ?
quiz.explain: Reversing the outer letters keeps Y in the middle: ∠ZYX.
steps: The vertex of ∠XYZ is Y, the middle letter.
Reversing the outer letters keeps Y in the middle: ∠ZYX.
∠YXZ, ∠XZY, ∠YZX have a different middle letter, so a different vertex.
So ∠ZYX is the same angle.
Answer: ∠ZYX
quiz.mistake: Moves the vertex out of the middle

quiz.q: Three rays OA, OB, OC start at O. Why is '∠O' not a good name?
options: Because O is not a point
Because there are three angles at O, so ∠O does not say which one
quiz.explain: ∠AOB, ∠BOC and ∠AOC all have vertex O, so we need three letters.
steps: With rays OA, OB, OC there are three angles at O: ∠AOB, ∠BOC, ∠AOC.
'∠O' does not tell which of these we mean.
So we must use three letters.
Answer: Because there are three angles at O, so ∠O does not say which one
quiz.mistake: Thinks one letter is always enough

quiz.q: What are the arms of ∠MNP?
quiz.explain: The arms start at the vertex N and go through M and P.
steps: In ∠MNP the vertex is N (middle letter).
The arms start at N and pass through M and through P.
So the arms are NM and NP.
Arms always start at the vertex.
Answer: NM and NP
quiz.mistake: Starts the arms at the wrong point

quiz.q: Rays OA, OB, OC, OD start at O. How many angles are formed (smaller than a straight angle, with arms on these rays)?
quiz.explain: ∠AOB, ∠AOC, ∠AOD, ∠BOC, ∠BOD, ∠COD: 6 angles.
steps: Pair each ray with every ray after it.
OA with OB, OC, OD → 3; OB with OC, OD → 2; OC with OD → 1.
So 6 angles are formed.
Answer: 6
quiz.mistake: Counts only the angles between neighbouring rays

quiz.q: Five rays start from one point, all inside a quarter turn. How many angles do they make?
steps: Pair each ray with every ray after it.
1st ray → 4 angles, 2nd → 3, 3rd → 2, 4th → 1.
So they make 10 angles.
Answer: 10
quiz.mistake: Counts only neighbours (4) or one per ray (5)

quiz.q: When Asha opens a pair of scissors, where is the vertex of the angle?
options: At the tips of the blades
At the screw where the blades meet
quiz.explain: The blades turn about the screw, so that is the common point of the arms.
steps: The two blades are the arms of the angle.
They turn about the screw where they are joined.
The common point of the arms is the vertex.
So the vertex is at the screw.
Answer: At the screw where the blades meet
quiz.mistake: Picks the tips, where the arms end

quiz.q: Which everyday thing does NOT show an angle opening and closing?
options: A door turning on its hinges
A ball rolling on the ground
quiz.explain: A rolling ball has no two arms turning about a point.
steps: An angle needs two arms turning about a point.
A door (hinge), a book (spine) and compasses (top joint) all have this.
A rolling ball has no two arms turning about a point.
So the rolling ball does not show an angle.
Answer: A ball rolling on the ground
quiz.mistake: Thinks anything that moves makes an angle

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: 'Why can't I just call every angle at point B ∠B?'
teach.praise: Chirp! With many angles at B, three letters with B in the middle say exactly which one!
teach.nudge: What happens when two or three angles share the same vertex?

revise.summary: An angle has a vertex and two arms, and is named with three letters with the vertex in the middle. When many angles share a vertex, three letters say exactly which angle is meant.
focus: Find the vertex and arms from an angle's name
Explain why ∠B alone can be unclear
Count all the angles made by several rays from one point
Spot angles in daily life (scissors, doors, clock hands)
remember: ∠ABC has vertex B and arms BA and BC; ∠CBA is the same angle
3 rays from O make ∠AOB, ∠BOC and ∠AOC
4 rays from one point make 6 angles; 5 rays make 10
traps: The vertex is the middle letter, not the first
Don't count only the angles between neighbouring rays
The vertex of open scissors is at the screw, not at the tips

learn.hook: Which slice of pizza is bigger? Put one on top of the other and see!
points: To compare two angles, place one on top of the other with the vertices together and one arm on top of the other arm.
The angle whose second arm sticks out further is bigger. If the second arms also match, the angles are equal.
Equal angles have the same amount of turn, even if they look different because of their position.
If you cannot move the angles, put a transparent circle with its centre on each vertex and mark where the arms cross it. More of the circle between the arms means a bigger angle.
Folding a paper makes creases and angles. Name them, then compare them to find the largest and smallest.

example.q: ∠A is put on ∠B with vertices together and one arm matching. The other arm of ∠A lies inside ∠B. Which is bigger?
steps: One pair of arms match.
∠A's other arm is inside ∠B, so ∠A turns less.
So ∠B is bigger.

learn.reallife: Tailors compare collar angles by laying one piece on another, and carpenters check corners by fitting a set-square.

games.title: Compare carefully
items: To compare angles, the vertices must be placed together.
Otherwise the turns cannot be matched.
An angle drawn with longer arms is always bigger.
Only the turn matters, not arm length.
If both arms match after superimposing, the angles are equal.
They have the same turn.
A transparent circle can compare angles that cannot be moved.
Compare how much of the circle lies between the arms.
An angle that looks tilted is smaller.
Turning an angle round does not change its size.

games.title: Smallest to biggest turn
items: A quarter of a right angle
Half a right angle
A right angle
Half a full turn
Three quarters of a full turn

quiz.q: Ravi superimposes ∠P on ∠Q with vertices and one arm matching. The other arm of ∠P is outside ∠Q. What can he say?
quiz.explain: ∠P turns further, so it is bigger.
steps: The vertices and one arm match.
The other arm of ∠P lies outside ∠Q.
So ∠P turns further than ∠Q.
∠P is bigger.
Answer: ∠P is bigger
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'outside' means smaller

quiz.q: When comparing two angles by putting one on the other, what must match first?
quiz.explain: Put the vertices together and lay one arm along the other arm.
steps: To compare, put one angle on top of the other.
First the vertices must match, and one arm must lie along the other arm.
Then see where the second arms fall.
Arm lengths, colours or letters do not matter.
Answer: The vertices and one arm
quiz.mistake: Lines up the arm ends instead of the vertices

quiz.q: ∠X = 40° is drawn with 2 cm arms, ∠Y = 40° with 9 cm arms but turned sideways. Which is true?
quiz.explain: Both have the same turn of 40°, so they are equal.
steps: Both angles measure 40°.
The size of an angle is the amount of turn, not the arm length or the way it faces.
So they are equal.
Answer: They are equal
quiz.mistake: Is fooled by arm length or position

quiz.q: Using a transparent circle centred at the vertex, ∠A covers 3 marks of the circle and ∠B covers 5 equal marks. Which is bigger?
quiz.explain: More of the circle between the arms means more turn, so ∠B is bigger.
steps: The circle is centred at the vertex and split into equal marks.
∠A covers 3 marks; ∠B covers 5 marks.
More marks between the arms = more turn.
So ∠B is bigger.
Answer: ∠B
quiz.mistake: Thinks fewer marks means bigger

quiz.q: Why do we centre the transparent circle on the vertex?
options: So the circle measures the turn about the vertex
Because arms must touch the edge
quiz.explain: The turn happens about the vertex, so the circle must be centred there.
steps: An angle is a turn about its vertex.
To measure that turn, the circle must be centred on the vertex.
Then the part of the circle between the arms shows the turn.
So we centre it to measure the turn about the vertex.
Answer: So the circle measures the turn about the vertex
quiz.mistake: Places the circle anywhere

quiz.q: A paper is folded once, then folded again so the first crease falls on itself. The two creases make four angles at the centre. What are they like?
quiz.explain: Folding the crease onto itself splits the straight angle into two equal halves, giving four right angles.
steps: The first fold makes a straight crease (a straight angle).
Folding the crease onto itself splits the straight angle into two equal halves.
Each half is a right angle, and the second crease makes four of them.
So all four are equal right angles.
Answer: All equal right angles
quiz.mistake: Does not see that the folds make equal halves

quiz.q: A fan has three angles between its blades. Two are equal and the third is larger. If the equal ones are 100° each, how big is the third?
quiz.explain: The three angles make a full turn: 360 − 100 − 100 = 160°.
steps: The three angles around the centre make a full turn: 360°.
Two angles are 100° each: 100 + 100 = 200°.
Third angle = 360 − 200 = 160°.
So the third angle is 160°.
Answer: 160°
quiz.mistake: Forgets the angles make a full turn

quiz.q: Meera says ∠ABC is bigger than ∠DEF because ∠ABC's arms are longer. What is her mistake?
options: Arm length does not decide the size of an angle
quiz.explain: Size is the amount of turn between the arms, not the arm length.
steps: The size of an angle is the amount of turn between its arms.
Longer arms do not mean more turn.
So Meera cannot say ∠ABC is bigger just because its arms are longer.
Her mistake: arm length does not decide the size of an angle.
Answer: Arm length does not decide the size of an angle
quiz.mistake: Judges angles by arm length

teach.ask: Gappu has two paper angles. 'How do I find which one is bigger?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Vertex on vertex, arm on arm, then see which other arm turns further!
teach.nudge: Where should the two angles touch when you put them together?

revise.summary: To compare two angles, place one on the other with vertices together and one arm on one arm; the one whose second arm sticks out further is bigger. Arm length and position do not change the size of an angle.
focus: Compare angles by superimposing: match vertices and one arm first
Use a transparent circle centred on the vertex to compare turns
Recognise equal angles even when arm lengths or positions differ
remember: Bigger angle: its second arm sticks out further when vertices and one arm match
Equal angles have the same amount of turn
More of the circle between the arms means a bigger angle
traps: Arm length does not decide the size of an angle
Don't line up the arm ends; line up the vertices and one arm
Don't place the circle anywhere: centre it on the vertex

topics.title: Angles as turns: right and straight angles

learn.hook: Two straws and a paper clip can make every angle there is!
points: Join two straws with a clip so one can turn: this rotating-arms model shows an angle as a turn.
To copy an angle cut as a slit, open the arms until they pass exactly through the slit. That opening is the same angle.
A straight angle is a half turn. Half of a straight angle is a right angle, a quarter turn.
Fold a paper once to get a straight edge, then fold that edge onto itself: the corner you get is a right angle.
On dot grids you can join points to make straight angles (three dots in a line) and right angles (like the corner of a square).

example.q: Rays OA, OB, OC, OD fan out from O, all inside a right angle. How many acute angles are there?
steps: Every angle between these rays is less than 90°, so all are acute.
So there are 6 acute angles.

learn.reallife: Opening a laptop lid, turning a door key and opening a gate all turn an arm about a point, just like the straw model.

items.q: Degrees in half a straight angle
Right angles in a straight angle
Right angles in a full turn
Acute angles made by 3 rays inside a right angle
Acute angles made by 4 rays inside a right angle
Acute angles made by 5 rays inside a right angle

games.title: Turn true or false
items: A right angle is half of a straight angle.
Folding a paper twice correctly makes a right angle.
The second fold halves the straight crease.
Opening the straw model wider makes a smaller angle.
More turn means a bigger angle.
Three dots in a straight row make a straight angle at the middle dot.
The two arms point in opposite directions.
Making the straws longer changes the angle.
Angle size does not depend on arm length.

quiz.q: A right angle is what part of a straight angle?
quiz.explain: A straight angle is 180° and a right angle is 90°: one half.
steps: Straight angle = 180°; right angle = 90°.
So a right angle is one half of a straight angle.
Answer: One half
quiz.mistake: Thinks a right angle is a quarter of a straight angle

quiz.q: How can you make a right angle with just a sheet of paper?
options: Fold it once, then fold the crease onto itself
quiz.explain: The first fold makes a straight edge; folding that onto itself halves it into right angles.
steps: Fold the paper once to get a straight edge (a straight angle).
Fold that crease onto itself.
This halves the straight angle, giving right angles.
So fold once, then fold the crease onto itself.
Answer: Fold it once, then fold the crease onto itself
quiz.mistake: Thinks one fold is enough

quiz.q: Sahil sets his straw model to pass through an angle-shaped slit cut in a card. What has he done?
options: Measured the length of the slit
Copied the angle of the slit
quiz.explain: When the arms just fit the slit, the model's opening equals the slit's angle.
steps: The straw model's arms are set to just fit the slit.
Then its opening matches the slit's opening.
So he has copied the angle of the slit.
He has not measured its length or made a straight angle.
Answer: Copied the angle of the slit
quiz.mistake: Thinks the model measures length

quiz.q: Six rays start from one point, all within a right angle. How many acute angles do they make?
quiz.explain: 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 15 acute angles.
steps: Six rays within a right angle: every pair makes an acute angle.
1st ray pairs with 5, 2nd with 4, 3rd with 3, 4th with 2, 5th with 1.
So they make 15 acute angles.
Answer: 15
quiz.mistake: Counts only neighbouring angles (5)

quiz.q: On a dot grid, which three dots make a straight angle at the middle dot B?

quiz.q: A clock's minute hand moves from 12 to 6. Through what angle does it turn?

Answer: 180°

quiz.q: How many right angles make one full turn?

The other goes up the column (straight up).
A row and a column meet like the corner of a square.
So the angle is a right angle.

learn.hook: How much does a door open? How far do clock hands turn? Degrees tell us exactly!
points: The size of an angle is the amount of turn between its arms. We measure it in degrees (°).

Using a protractor: put its centre on the vertex, line up the baseline with one arm, and read the scale that starts at 0 on that arm.
Longer or shorter arms do not change the angle. Only the opening matters.
On a clock, the hour marks are 360° ÷ 12 = 30° apart.

learn.hook: Why not 100 degrees in a circle? Nobody knows for sure, but there are some clever ideas!
points: Nobody knows for sure why we use 360. One idea: many ancient calendars (in India, Persia, Babylonia and Egypt) used a year of 360 days. Another: the Babylonians counted in sixties (base 60), and 360 = 6 × 60.
360 has many divisors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 15, 18, 20, ... So a full turn splits into many equal whole-number angles.
Each equal part of a circle split into n parts is 360° ÷ n: 2 parts → 180°, 3 → 120°, 4 → 90°, 5 → 72°, 6 → 60°, 8 → 45°, 9 → 40°, 10 → 36°, 12 → 30°.
A paper protractor: fold a paper circle in half (180°), again (90°), again (45°) and once more (22½°). Mark the creases to measure angles roughly.

360 is not prime, not the biggest number and not a palindrome.

quiz.q: A ray bisects a 110° angle. What is each part?

Each part = 110 ÷ 2.
So each part is 55°.

quiz.q: How can you find the bisector of an angle drawn on paper without a protractor?

Fold the paper so one arm lies exactly on the other arm.
The crease through the vertex divides the angle equally.
So the crease is the bisector.
Answer: Fold so the two arms lie on each other; the crease is the bisector

quiz.q: Two lines cross so that all four angles are right angles. What are these lines called?
quiz.explain: Lines that meet at right angles are perpendicular. Parallel lines never meet at all.
steps: The lines meet so that all four angles are right angles.
Lines meeting at right angles are perpendicular.
Parallel lines never meet at all.
So they are perpendicular lines.
Answer: Perpendicular lines
quiz.mistake: Confuses perpendicular with parallel

quiz.q: Joseph says the smaller angle between the clock hands at 10:00 is obtuse. Is he right?
options: No, it is a right angle
No, it is 60°, an acute angle
quiz.explain: From 10 to 12 is 2 hour-gaps: 2 × 30° = 60°, which is acute.
steps: Count hour-gaps the short way: 10 → 11 → 12 = 2
60° < 90°, so acute
Answer: No, it is 60°, an acute angle
quiz.mistake: Counts the gaps the long way round or miscounts

quiz.q: An angle is split into two equal parts of 50° each. What type is the whole angle?
quiz.explain: The whole angle is 50° + 50° = 100°, which is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse.
steps: Answer: Obtuse
quiz.mistake: Looks at one part (50°, acute) instead of the whole angle

teach.ask: Gappu flaps: 'Acute, right, obtuse, straight... how do I tell which is which?'
teach.praise: Yay! Less than 90° is acute, exactly 90° is right, between 90° and 180° is obtuse, 180° is straight. I'm an angle expert!
teach.nudge: What number do I compare the angle with to decide its type?

revise.summary: Angles are named by size: acute (less than 90°), right (exactly 90°), obtuse (between 90° and 180°), straight (exactly 180°) and reflex (between 180° and 360°). Lines meeting at a right angle are perpendicular.
focus: Classify an angle from its degree measure
Find clock-hand angles and then name their type
Know that perpendicular lines meet at a right angle
remember: Acute: more than 0° but less than 90°; right: exactly 90°
Obtuse: more than 90° but less than 180°; straight: exactly 180°
Reflex: more than 180° but less than 360°
traps: Not every angle over 90° is reflex: 170° is obtuse
A flat, open book makes a straight angle, not a right angle
Don't confuse perpendicular with parallel

learn.hook: The Ashoka Chakra on our flag hides a neat angle puzzle!
points: Two angles that sit side by side on a straight line add up to 180°. If one is 130°, the other is 50°.
Letters can be drawn using given angles: the letter M has two slanting middle strokes; the letter Y has a stem and two arms making angles at the joint.
The angles around a point add to 360°. Around the joint of the letter Y, the three angles make a full turn.
The Ashoka Chakra has 24 equally spaced spokes, so the angle between neighbouring spokes is 360° ÷ 24 = 15°.

example.q: A ray stands on a straight line making a 65° angle. Find the other angle on the line.
steps: The two angles together make 180°.
The other angle is 115°.

learn.reallife: A ladder against a wall, a seesaw and a half-open gate all make two angles on a straight line that add to 180°.

quiz.q: A ray on a straight line makes angles of 72° and x. What is x?
steps: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.
Answer: 108°
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 90 or 360

quiz.q: What is the angle between two neighbouring spokes of the Ashoka Chakra (24 spokes)?
steps: 24 spokes split a full turn (360°) into 24 equal gaps.
So neighbouring spokes are 15° apart.
Answer: 15°
quiz.mistake: Uses 180 instead of 360

quiz.q: In the Ashoka Chakra, what is the angle between one spoke and the spoke 6 places away?
quiz.explain: 6 gaps of 15° each = 90°.
steps: Each gap between neighbouring spokes = 15°.
6 places away = 6 gaps.
So the angle is 90°.
Answer: 90°
quiz.mistake: Counts spokes instead of gaps

quiz.q: Two angles on a straight line are equal. What is each?
quiz.explain: 180 ÷ 2 = 90°, so each is a right angle.
steps: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.
Two equal angles: each = 180 ÷ 2.
So each is a right angle, 90°.
Answer: 90°
quiz.mistake: Halves 90 instead of 180

quiz.q: A see-saw plank makes an angle of 35° with the ground on one side. What angle does it make on the other side (along the ground line)?
quiz.explain: The two angles on the straight ground add to 180°: 180 − 35 = 145°.
steps: The two angles on the straight ground line add up to 180°.
One angle = 35°.
Other angle = 180 − 35 = 145°.
So it makes 145° on the other side.
Answer: 145°
quiz.mistake: Thinks they must be equal

quiz.q: In the letter Y, the stem makes 150° with each arm. What is the angle between the two arms?
quiz.explain: The angles round the joint make 360°: 360 − 150 − 150 = 60°.
steps: Answer: 60°
quiz.mistake: Uses 180 instead of 360

quiz.q: Three angles sit side by side on a straight line: 40°, 75° and x. What is x?
steps: Answer: 65°
quiz.mistake: Forgets one of the angles

quiz.q: Zoya draws the letter M with straight up-and-down outer strokes. What kind of angle is at each top corner?
quiz.explain: Each top corner of M is a sharp point, so the angle is less than 90°.
steps: The outer strokes go straight up and down.
The slanting middle stroke meets each outer stroke at a sharp point at the top.
A sharp point is less than 90°.
So each top corner is acute.
Answer: Acute
quiz.mistake: Thinks the corners of M are right angles

teach.ask: Gappu sits on a straight branch. A twig makes 50° with it. 'What angle is on the other side?'
teach.praise: Tweet! 180 − 50 = 130°. A straight line always shares 180°!
teach.nudge: What do the two angles on a straight line add up to?

revise.summary: Angles side by side on a straight line add up to 180°, and angles around a point add up to 360°. The Ashoka Chakra's 24 equal spokes are 15° apart.
focus: Find a missing angle on a straight line using 180°
Find a missing angle around a point using 360°
Count gaps, not spokes, when finding angles on the Ashoka Chakra
remember: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°
Angles around a point add up to 360°
Ashoka Chakra: 360° ÷ 24 = 15°
traps: On a straight line, subtract from 180, not 90 or 360
Around a point (like the joint of Y), use 360, not 180
Two equal angles on a line are 90° each, not 45°
